I think I turned 14 last week, Nana. Not a lawyer. More like a prime minister!      A prime minister who’s currently Googling “how to fold socks” and still hasn’t found the shop.      Come on, we need socks, not therapy!      Here it is, here it is! That red sign there—Mother Care. Doesn’t look like it was updated since 1993?      That’s because it wasn’t. But the stock’s still better than the shops in London. Silly British people—charging double for a pack of toilets and calling it a ‘big save’.     We don’t have to go to London. We’re in Preston!      Hey, you weren’t born here! You come from Prime Minister Street in about nowhere, London. Pronounced "Pred-nowhere", according to your lingo.      It’s  Primrose  Street and it is  not  in nowhere. My grandma’s got better hair than your guest speaker last year.      Let's just all agree the socks come first, then maybe we can sort out who has better grandmas.      Deal. Now, first stop—blankets aisle. They got the big, fluffy ones you can wrap a whole sofa in?      I bet they have the kind you suffocate in.      Which, let’s face it, is a big win in winter.      Right, I’ll pick out the best one. We’ll start with that and then move on to the essentials: toothpaste, batteries, and baby wipes—just in case.      Oh! We should check for baby stuff too. I heard you’re trying to start something new soon?      It’s not confirmed yet, but maybe. Should I just go around the house with a blanket and start nestling on the couch?      Nana! That’s so weird to hear.

So do you play The Legend of Zelda on your phone gramma?      No, love... I don’t even know what that is. I don’t have a phone like that. All I’ve got is my £20 mobile from the shop—just for texts and calls.      That’s  not  a bad thing, really. My phone basically exploded once because of a game.      Not funny! Why'd it explode?      It’s exaggeration. A bit. But I did once drop it in a hotdog.      Oh, dear! Still, I like my simplicity. All I need is to call my sister, and now and then visit a bit of Facebook—just to see what the grandkids are up to.      But Gramma, there are little games even you can try! My teacher says it’s good for your brain if you do a bit of puzzle stuff online. Like crosswords, or Sudoku.      I do the newspaper crossword every morning, love. I’ve been doing it for 30 years. I don’t need a screen for that.      Huh. Tell that to my brain—it would probably say "thanks," then fall asleep.      Should I show you my game?      What’s it called?       Bridging the Gap . It’s a logic puzzle where you connect islands by drawing bridges—but there are rules!      Like rush hour for oddly-shaped bits of land?      Sort of! It’s not as bad as it sounds. I’ve done 200 levels already. It helps with your mood, apparently.      And what makes you say that?      My psychology teacher. She said games can help with anxiety, like for people who get stressed about exams or work.      Work? Love, you’re not working yet.      I know, I’m doing AS levels, but I  am  going to work soon. At university. Or a lab or something related to science.       That  I can believe. She’s basically a human go-to for random facts.      Just don’t go into dentistry, yeah? You might be the one drilling the wrong bit again.      That was  one  time, and it was virtual!      But it was virtual  in front of the entire class .      It wasn’t the  virtual  part that was bad. It was the laughing.      Well, don’t you worry about that now. It’s almost Christmas, and I reckon you’ll be wondering what to buy your poor, possibly traumatized boyfriend for the holidays.      It’s fine. I just need a really convincing chocolate cake recipe this year.

Right, so today we're talking about metals and fabrics, just like we've done in class. Do you know what metal coins are often made of?      Copper?      Good guess! Some coins are, but in Minecraft you mostly find things like iron and copper when you dig underground.      I have a big pile of iron in my inventory! I made a pickaxe too.      Well done, love. Iron is super useful. It’s one of the first strong metals you get. Do you want to know what even stronger ones are like?      What’s stronger than iron?      There’s gold, but it breaks quicker, even though it shines. Then later on you get to dig for diamonds, which are the strongest. Oh, and there’s even netherite if you find the right place. But that’s more advanced.      I don’t want gold. I want hides! They make the best boots so I don’t die in lava!      You know, in real life too, hides and fabrics are super important. Hides from animals can be made into leather, which is tough.      Like our clothes?      Exactly! Sometimes, like in colder countries, people used to wear a lot of wool because it keeps them warm. You know what wool is?      Yes! Sheep have it!      Perfect! And sheep aren’t just for wool – they’re also very fluffy and cute. In real life and in Minecraft!      Ooh, I have a sheep in my game! I just watched it jump over a fence. It’s a funny sheep!      That sounds like it might be a special one! In Minecraft, they can do funny things if you play in creative mode.      Are there any other special animals?      Oh, plenty! There are invented legends, such as dragons that breathe fire or cats that never meow but just follow you around with evil eyes. Some people invent these characters for stories, even around animals and metals!      I have a dragon in my game!      Oh, cool! How was it invented in your game?      It came from a chest in a pyramid. I opened it and poof – dragon!      That’s made-up, but adventurers in stories do find things like that. Dragons are very legendary!      My new cat is soft. She’s black like night.      Nice! It’s important to take good care of her. You should also make sure you’re taking your vitamins, just like the grown-ups do, so you stay strong and healthy.

So did you go see that gig last weekend at the old warehouse? The one with the punk band?      Nah, I was at my cousin’s birthday. But I heard it was proper mad – someone chucked a boot at the lead singer!      No way! I saw the footage online. He caught it mid-air and just looked at it like  “What? I’ve been through worse.”       Haha, typical. Imagine going through that as a lead singer. You’re like the centre of the world when you're on stage.      Honestly, I'd still play. I've been thinking of picking up a guitar again. Just never had the discipline. You’ve already got one left in the storage unit – I saw you lugging it in after the last open mic night.      Yeah, eventually I’ll practice. I just haven’t been inspired since everyone has been off in other cities. It’s not the same without my mates to jam with.      That’s why I said we should start a band again. We used to be decent! Remember the time we did that cover of  Smells Like Teen Spirit  in the back room of that bar where we first met? You sang so much – Matey nearly got deaf!      Oh yeah, the time he nearly picked up a bottle and through it at the amp. And we were only 18! Honestly, feels like a decade ago.      Feels like yesterday. I mean, what made you decide to drop your music and start all that college jazz?      Erm, I did it for respect. My dad kept bugging me to  “get a real job.”  So I thought, “Okay, let me do the boring thing so he leaves me to do the fun stuff on the side.”      Haha, and? Has it worked?      Not really. He just focuses on when I’m doing nothing. It’s like he can’t win. And also, trying to find landlords who allow musical instruments is the worst.      Tell me about it. Try explaining the number of guitars in your room on your council housing application.      I just ticked “other” and wrote “paedophiles hate them due to their size and shape.”      You’re mental.      You love me for it.      I do, to an extent. I’m not entirely sure if I like that joke. My nan would have had a fit, and my friend Karen definitely backs out of the table now when we start talking about it.

So did you lot hear about this EPQ thing? My teacher’s been going on about it like it’s the be-all and end-all of sixth form.      Yeah, I mean, it is kind of important if you want to do a degree at a top uni. But I don’t get how we’re meant to come up with an idea. I reckon mine should be all about how schools can fight food poverty. My brother’s got free school meals but he still goes hungry sometimes.      That’s actually a really good idea. Didn’t your mum use to volunteer at the food bank in Wembley?      Yeah, and I saw how much effort it takes to get the food out. You know, like, not just the logistics of it, but the stigma around using them too. People say it’s the government’s job, but it’s not really working.      I dunno. Maybe mine should be something a bit more fun. Like, I’ve always wanted to try juggling. Maybe why people like watching performers—like circus stuff, street performers. That’d be cool. I mean, we’re going to Montenegro for a holiday in July, right? Maybe I can watch how people busk there and write about it.      Busking in Montenegro sounds way more exciting than sitting in a lecture hall. Have you thought about uni yet? I want to do something related to humanitarianism. Like, maybe development studies or someone who works in organisations that help with emergency stuff—like after earthquakes or floods.      That’s a proper stretch from normal sixth form subjects, but I get it. You’re into saving people, aren’t you?      Kind of. I just hate seeing stuff on the news and not being able to help. I mean, if unis are all about personal growth, I’d rather grow into someone who can do that than someone who knows all the laws on the planet.      Okay, but what about money? Like, how much is all this going to cost? I’ve seen how expensive some of the uni courses are. If I do arts-related stuff, I might be stuck delivering pizza forever.      That’s the problem with being British, innit? You work your ass off at school and then suddenly, it’s like the box got taken away from you.      I mean, at least we’re not in Slough or Wembley doing that, right?

Honestly, I don't know how anyone expects to study in this place. Our internet's slower than a snail in treacle half the time. I’m uploading a whole essay and it’s taking  ages  to do 5%.      Don’t get me started. I was trying to stream a lecture earlier, and it cut out every five minutes. I looked like I was having a mental breakdown with that buffering wheel. At least the sofa doesn’t squeak like in our last flat though, which is something.      You lot are lucky your flat isn’t rented by some dodgy guy who makes weird baked goods. Last week I left my room and the supply of samosas in the kitchen had  doubled . I’m not even gonna ask how.      You're all too picky. The lights don’t flicker in ours, at least. Remember what it was like in that dorm? I mean, I saw a  spider the size of my phone  once, and the landlord couldn’t even care less.      I know, right? We need to write to the uni again about the broken heating. It’s  October  for goodness’ sake, and it feels like we’ve got a fridge in our living room.      Don't mention it, least we’ve got  more  room than my flatmate. Three of us sharing a single. If I sneeze once more while she's brushing her teeth at someone o'clock in the morning, I swear my head's gonna explode.      Yeah, but at least in your case the bathroom stays warm. I once had to wait  ten minutes  in about five degrees to walk to the toilet. And it wasn’t because I had to queue — no, the person inside was doing their hair and they didn’t want the  hot air to dry out their ‘edge’  or whatever.      That’s bad. I don’t mind a few dodgy microwave sounds or weird smells, but if your living room could frost up, that’s not cool. Even  I  would lose it.      Okay, but the best part of uni is still the gossip. Did you hear the one about Sarah goading her flatmate into a bet about who could go one week without speaking to anyone? It went  horribly  wrong when the other one stopped emerging from her room. Sarah said it was for “her own good” after she spilled tea on her keyboard…

So did you manage to sort out the Christmas plans with Niel’s sister? I know she’s been on about it for weeks.      Yes and no! We finally got a reply last week, but it turns out she’s having the in-laws over for the entire week, so we had to backtrack and sort out something with Ruth instead. Which is fine, honestly—Ruth’s place is a bit bigger, and I think the kids will enjoy the change.      Ruth, the one from Porthmadog? I remember her dragging me outside when I was still in Wales to show me the cow she had as a kid—what was its name again?      Clwyd? Or Cwm? I’m still not sure. It tried to bite her once and then lived in a shed for the rest of its life. But Ruth’s actually brilliant with the kids, better than I am—she doesn’t mind the mess, which I’m eternally grateful for.      You always say that, but I’m fairly sure that shed was one of the most hygienically challenged places I’ve ever been in. Was it even allowed to be a shed for a cow?      Let’s not go there. So anyway, Ruth’s doing a big festive dinner, and she’s asked if Hayley and Freddie can come over on the 26th for their usual afternoon spotting reindeer in the garden and trying to invent snow from the hose. Oh and Niel’s sister’s daughter is coming with her brother—smaller kids—so Ruth said she’ll be able to handle the double tea-time chaos.      Ooh, I love how excited Hayley gets about "the man in the red coat." It’s like a mission for her. Has Freddie figured that out yet or is it still a mystery?      He thinks Father Snowy is a real thing. I tried to tell him it was a bit of a myth, but all he said was, “But you always say he brought your birthday present.” So I had to shut up. And also, trying to find a holiday job in Exeter was such a nightmare. I ended up teaching a couple of Thai teenagers via Zoom the week before term go back. I think their Thai is better now than mine.      Oh no, I bet. You’re not bad though—I remember your conversation with that older woman from Ankara in the corner of the bar last year.

Dad, I can't believe we're finally doing this. Like, it's been  ages .      Aye, it's like more than I can count on one hand. Where's this flat of yours anyway? Still Bedford?      No, I’ve actually moved to Brighton. Thought I’d get a bit of sea air and maybe some proper culture.      Aye, Brighton’s alright if you like pasty BME types and hippies, eh?      Very funny. Funny how you still can’t say “BME” without like, rolling your eyes. Not everything is a joke, Dad.      Alright, well what’s the address? I’m not getting left behind on this backroad somewhere. I still remember the last time I was lost in Bedford. Some inspector gave me a ticket because I parked on a yellow line, and I swear I was just doing my shopping for five minutes.      That’s because you parked near the speed camera. And I think your license is still suspended for that, remember?      I never got the letter. They must’ve sent it to the old address. Good times…      Yeah, but you’re still okay at –?      At least I know the way to the pub. That’s not in question. Speaking of which, will there be drinks when we get there?      If you survive the drive. Let me test my phone a sec – did I remember the recording app?      What? You still got that thing on? I thought you stopped doing that research after about five minutes.      No, it’s for an English class project. My students are obsessed with family conversations. Supposed to show how unfiltered people are around the ones they love.      Aye, well here’s to bad language and worse driving then. Go on, ask me something intense to get you some juicy data.      Right… Okay, how did you feel when I first told you I was teaching English in Africa? Was it… weird for you?      Aye, it was. First I thought you were off your head. Going to Tanzania? With all the bugs and that. But then I saw your face on that video your mum forwarded. You looked healthy enough. Smiling. Thought maybe you’d finally found something decent to do with your life.      Thanks, Dad. That means a lot. It  was  tough at first. I mean, I was alone, kind of. But it reshaped things for me. Met some good people.      Aye, you always said you wanted to help people.

So did you manage to sort out that public relations meeting with the student societies today?      Yeah, I did—went reasonably well. One of the football clubs had a bit of a meltdown over their new Instagram account. They thought the admin had posted a swear word by accident, but it was just a slang term from the 80s.           Oh dear. A lot of people would panic over that. I had a meeting with the records office today about someone requesting their past coursework. Turns out the system doesn’t chase archived papers the way it used to. I had to go old school and print everything off.      Ugh, I miss the days of paper trails. You know you’re getting left behind when you start calling the IT guy for help, only to pick up a pen and paper and just— write it down instead.       Exactly. I even found some of my old lecture notes in the drawer. I looked at one, thinking it’s for a seminar I still teach, and it was like reading someone else’s handwriting—personally, violently critical of my younger self.      I tell you, reading my early teaching evaluations… I would’ve quit. I remember when I got “passive” as feedback. I was fairly proud of it, because I thought being low-key was chill. Now I know that “passive” means I didn’t speak for ten minutes while the students looked at each other panicking.   :   I had a similar one. “Approachable but distant.” What does  that  even mean?      You know what about you today? You mentioned the coffee machine the other week. Have you had it fixed yet?      Not yet! I rang the guy who does the local café, and he’s overbooked until Wednesday. But I passed Nordstrom’s on the way home and the biscuits there were on offer, so I brought some back. I know your coffee break is sacrosanct, and I wanted to soften the blow.      Thank you! That was extremely thoughtful. I’ve been trying to reduce sugar intake but these are the ones with almonds in them. I’ll suffer if necessary.      I figured. Oh, and I might be dragging you to the record shop at some point this week. I have a fluency test on Friday and decided it’d help to listen to something with strong regional accents to prepare.      Like the Cumbrian folk singer I once took you to see in Keswick?

So do you think I've done this right? I mean I've got this pattern it's like a like a daisy and it's got a pale pink sort of background.      Yeah I mean it looks good. You've only just started it as well. You'll get better as you go on.      Yeah I was just wondering if if it's not too complicated for a first-time knitter cos I think I knitted this first row wrong somehow and it makes it quite wobbly.      Well the first row never looks great, but the second row looks fine.      Yeah I made sure I corrected it. What I'm going to do is make like a squishy beanbag out of it and then put a book inside or something to make it into a bolster, push it into the corner of the sofa to make it look nice.      That sounds good. I've been thinking about making some little throw cushions for the living room as well but I can't find spare fabric so maybe we could do them at the same time.      Yeah I mean I can I can sort of trace a pattern from this one and tell you how to do it.      That'd be good then. I mean it's good for me to get out the sewing machine and actually do something other than typing emails into a spreadsheet all day.      You know what I was thinking about as well though, is the bathroom. We've got one of those sort of solid shower curtains and it just looks oddly industrial. I was thinking about doing something similar with a stretchy cotton and putting some quilting in the corners to hold it up and have about five square feet of knitted daisies.      Oh I like that idea. That would transform that whole area. I mean it is a bit run-down to be honest.      Yeah it's not much better than ours was when we first bought the house. I was thinking as well about maybe putting a little frame on the wall with some stick-on shelves and a few yellow vases of dried flowers to add some softness.      That sounds really good. You think you'd get around to it or do you need me to go out and get stuff?      Just give me a couple of weeks, I'll manage.

Rather annoying isn't it, eh?      Well I know it's not real letters like it used to be, but still—someone should be keeping a bit of an eye on where we are and doing a bit more to help those in need.      We've talked about it eenough times at the council meetings. It's all good theory and clever ideas on paper, but most a' it don’t ever get done before they're off again.      It's not just that. We've had three different people from the borough office in the last month asking about my housing benefit like they didn’t even talk to each other. I've had to tell them the same story thrice now.      It's enough to make you lose your marbles, isn't it? D’you know, I think the world is run by people who’ve never had to worry about paying a bill—how d’they understand our situation?      I hear you, Mabel, but even if I had the time, I wouldn’t go near that lot with a ten-foot pole. Too busy running this place I keep in the High Street as it is. And tell me, what good would it do anyway?      Well, from what I hear, at least  someone  got a deal done in the council chambers the other day. They're talking about building more homes again—now that’s a load of nonsense if ever I heard one. There’s no way someone at the top is actually paying for it out of their own pocket.      Let’s not kid ourselves. It’s all talk and no action. I’ve had enough people knocking on my door in about forty years asking after a child’s head lice or what time Charlie had his tea.      You were better off at it than me, Mabel. I never had the patience for that lot. If you tell me someone passed out in the street and I'm to go collect them and give ‘em tea and sandwiches, no way. Not when I've got a shop to run and people that actually  pay me  to ignore their lunches.      That’s the difference, isn't it? Some of us had it, some of us didn’t go that way. But life doesn’t hand anyone a silver spoon, nor does it give anyone a second chance. Once you’re in the muck, your legs forget how to run.

Rather skip the newfit incense. You know what that smelt like? Like a caravan that's been burned out and then left out in the rain for a few months! Honestly, someone needs to tell them where the scent department is.      Yeah, well Martha went mad for it when I bought it for her last month. She was like, “Oh, it's all so natural!” I said yeah, natural, but not in that way.      It was quite interesting, actually. We had to test the samples for the new copy campaign, and the incense came specially imported from, like, some wellness village in Bulgaria. I swear someone must've taken hippie culture to the extreme and then sold it back to us with a premium price.      I reckon you're all too picky. If it relaxes you then you're meant to like it. I burned a stick of that stuff earlier this week and fell asleep for three hours. That’s gold dust as far as I’m concerned.      That’s because you were exhausted from the night shift. I don’t think it takes much to send you out.      It’s funny how much we buy in to these little things, isn’t it? Martha got herself a matching candle – same weird aroma – and I almost had to take her to a chemist the next day because of a migraine.      Honestly, I don’t get the obsession with fake 'wellness' stuff. But also, maybe not everyone has a sense of smell like you do, Speke. Some people find it calming and that’s it. I mean, does it matter in the grand scheme of things?      I suppose not. But when it costs fiver a stick and you could get something decent for that price... I mean, if I was going to burn something, I’d prefer the stuff you burn at Dad’s place during Christmas. The one that actually smells like it was made in a wooden workshop.      Oh bless, that’s the crackling applewood and cinnamon one.      Yeah, that one actually whiffs like someone took an apple pie, set it near a fire, and thought it smelled good. That goody really works for me if I’m stressed about work.      I’m actually planning a bit of a staycation soon. Maybe some self-care. I’m thinking I’ll buy a few nicer candles, some herbal tea, maybe even try not burning anything to death on the way.

Rather annoying isn't it, this weather.      You think it's bad in Larnaca, I've had worse in Ramsgate. I used to live by the coast, years and years ago. Not quite as hot, but the winds!      Yeah, I'm used to Dorset weather. It was actually   really   nice today when I got up, a bit warm, not too humid.      No, it does ease up in the morning. Today wasn't too bad. I like this place, though, don't you? You don’t often wander far enough out here to escape the touristy parts.      Oh yes, that’s true. I came here with a group last week, and most of them didn’t want to leave the Khyber Pass in De Korte. They said it was far too quiet around here. I, um… actually prefer this.      Me too, you ever spent much time on the island before?      Not too much—just one or two holidays a decade or so. My husband and I used to come every couple of years. Now I tend to come more for work. I teach English part-time.      Excellent. I remember when it was much more off-limits, you had to be careful where you went. Now it's all very… easy.      It’s changed a lot, yes. I mean, in the village I’m staying in, there are buses, there are markets, there’s internet. It is a   very   different Northern Cyprus to what most people imagine!      I did some consultancy work years back in Famagusta area, near the Buffer Zone. It was wild back then. You know that place used to be called Varosha, right?      Oh yeah, I’ve heard of it. Still cut off, isn't it? I remember hearing something on the news last year about people trying to go in.      Mmm. Some of the old hotels are still standing but no one lives there anymore. They're trying to let it reform naturally, I think.      That must go back to the 1970s, or earlier?      Oh definitely. I remember a bloke I used to work with had a cousin who owned a little restaurant there. Thought he’d never get it back after all those years. It was a right laugh tracking down the paperwork over thirty years.      That’s extraordinary. I had no idea.      You want to hear something even stranger? I met a guy once in Limassol who used to live in Nicosia as a child.

Rather skip the new bar and go to our usual one, do you think.      Yeah.      Just went there today with Cass I think it's probably a bit dirty.      Hmm.      It's got like a mossy smell in there.      Yeah I was going to say if it's not actually toxic.      It is but just generally that kind of place, um unpleasant but very cheap.      We can't be doing.      It's the only place that serves vodka like three yuan a glass.      Yeah.      You know and like that My turkey still cost me fifty seven yuan though left it on the back burner I didn't like the look of it.      Mm.      Mm better safe than sorry.      Mm.      I'm ever so grateful we found this building.      Mm.      It's got a nice feel.      Yeah.      It's only ten blocks from the university but on a main street.      Yeah got utility is key at the moment.      Yeah.      We were like oh no don't go out like this Sila was meant to be meeting us at that bar, huh.      Yeah.      So.      I think what you had to do.      Anyhow.      Yeah.      It's quite walkable the area round the university here.      Yeah what's your take.      I mean it is a student city but it's just, like for us, it's not.      Yeah and it's not as it is a cul-de-sac type of feel to it you know when you sort of stick out from the rest and that's what we were getting here.      Yeah.      Yeah no, you don't get that with our building it's all very connected go straight up on the main street.      Mm.      You don't go further than that.      Yeah.      Yeah but it's quite it's quite cheap to live here even for this type of area.      Yeah.      It's a very bleak kind of feeling to it.      Yeah.      It's not like very many trees or anything and the sky used to be just like you could.      Mm.      But you can't anymore. With that pollution on it.      It's strange here you don't get to see it that often unless there's a good.      Deliberately chose like orange because well it's a bit risky but it's rather vibrant.      Yeah I was just going to say your coat looks quite bright.      Yeah I've.      I think it looks quite good on you.

Right, I just took the chicken out of the oven. It’s still a bit early, but I wanted to get the smells going so no one forgets to come down! Any idea what we’re doing for dessert?      No, I didn’t plan anything. If you haven’t got it on, I say we go with the trifle from the fridge. It’s not as good as a pudding you’ve made from scratch, but I’d argue it isn’t far off either.      Oh, can we have the chocolate mousse instead? The one from the deli in Ashford? I brought it back from my lunch run today. I think we’ve earned it.      That’s a good idea, actually! The mousse would be nicer and more of a treat. You saved us, Laura. I was thinking the trifle was a bit too much like hard work.      Fair enough. Let’s go with the mousse. And I for one am grateful Laura remembered to bring back something that tastes like it came from a real patisserie and not a shelf.      Haha, don’t worry, I did bring back a few other things too. There’s some local ale for you, Derek, and then a few snacks from the farmer’s market. I got fairly sidetracked, but nothing’s been wasted.      Bless you, love. Silly of me to expect anything less! By the way, did you hear someone got cast in that TV show you auditioned for? It was one of those new BBC drama things about the law.      Oh, no! I missed the update notifications, but I assume it was someone from university. Everyone I used to know seems to be getting on to something. I’ve only been writing freelance copy for the past few months and it still feels like I’m scraping the surface.      Don’t put yourself down, love. You’re doing brilliantly. You’ve got a great eye for it. I still remember when you wrote that article on seasonal eating. It got hundreds of shares on Facebook. Websites were linking to it!      Ah, thank you, Meg. That means a lot coming from you. Sometimes I wonder if I’m in the right line of work, you know? But then I think about the line of work you’re in and I go, blooming hell, what would we do without nurses?      That’s the spirit!

Have you heard about the new bus route?      No, what’s that about?      It’s this new bus that goes directly from the city centre over to the Kettle’s Yard side of things. Supposedly, it's supposed to help with connectivity for students and all that. But honestly, I think they just handed over the contract to the lowest bidder again. I’ve been on it once and swore the driver was confused about where to turn.      Oh, wasn’t that the same bus company that tried to rebrand but still had the same grumpy guy behind the wheel as twenty years ago?      Yeah, that’s the one. It’s like a time machine back to 2003. Ten more years and the bus will probably start spewing smoke and knocking itself out of gear.      On a different note, have you been up to the Cambridge University Press bookshop lately?      No, why?      Oh, I popped in the other day and it’s changed a fair bit. They’ve got this section with all the student textbooks and academic grief. It's like walking into a library… but for people who have second thoughts about buying the “Essential History of Philosophy” book at the last second and then take the whole day deciding.      Sounds like them. I once met a guy who stood there for an hour, just comparing two different editions of Spinoza. At the end, he said, “I think I’ll buy the flimsier one because it costs less to send home.” Made no sense, but fair enough.      Yeah, and I think they’re having problems with student protesters this term. I overheard some of the workers talking about how the new ones are even more unrelenting than usual. Something about ‘ethical print policies’ or something.      Oh, come on. They can’t possibly be as bad as last year’s lot, who tried to station a mattress shop outside the building and then expected to get a discount.      At least they’re not trying to set themselves on fire this time. That’s a win.      Honestly, I think it’s more of a Cambridge phenomenon. I was at a student café in Manchester once and saw a box of granola displayed near your actual meals like it was some kind of statement. I was like, “Excuse me, I think you accidentally brought your healthy eating protest into the wrong place.”

So did you girls find the café okay? That part of Cheshire looks like it's grown since I was last there, and I'm not great with road signs. I got turned around once after a family wedding and ended up in Liverpool!      Oh you were never great with directions, Mary. I'm surprised you didn't end up somewhere in Wales by mistake. Anyway, we found "The Fox and Hound" all right. The pie was good and the coffee was hot, which was a plus.      It was lovely. The woman who served us, she had a lovely local accent, like, very old-fashioned Lakelander. She kept talking about the “good ol’ days” and how everyone knew each other around here back then. Fun to listen to, really. I think I would’ve liked her as a teacher.      Aye, it’s true. Those old-fashioned breakfasts and old-fashioned values, they were something alright. The hard part was looking after five children while we talked, didn’t it, Diane?      It was a circus, honestly, but we loved it. My little one, Elsie, said “I like nan and grand-uni” today. I was like—what does that even mean?      Oh, she just means you, right? “Grand-nan” for me and “grand-uni” for you? It’s all very confusing. I understand one language—maths. Everything else? Well, someone at the dinner table might as well be speaking French for all I understand.      Just the other day, Sam came over and asked where the Wi-Fi password was. He nearly about face-dropped when I said "write the word 'tablespoon' backwards and add a 7 at the end!" Not that I’d ever dream of doing that, but it’s just a joke for the look on his face.      A bit harsh, Kath. I remember when he was here last time, I tried to make him understand the English “craic” as in “how’s the craic?” He just looked puzzled and asked “are we in a pub?”      Aye, but that’s the fun of it. You lot get your life together and start a family, and I’m just left in the past trying to teach algebra in my head until the kids stop coming to visit. So how is work, Diane? Still writing and editing?      Yeah, I love it to be honest. I’ve been doing some transcription work for a local hospital.

Rather annoying isn't it, how they've put up all these chain-link fences around the river? You couldn't throw a pebble into the Thames now without feeling like a smuggler or something.      Yeah, quite the security operation. I bet it's all about preventing drone take-offs and dodgy picnics. Still, look at the view over there—can you believe that's the O2? A big, shiny spaceship sitting in the middle of a nondescript grass bank.      It's either the most modern building in the country or the most gloriously out of place. I mean, even Disney couldn’t imagine something so aggressively round and futuristic, and they’ve got Mickey’s nose to think about.      I remember when they put it up—everyone moaned for about a decade. "Afraid of the sea, aren’t we?!” Now it doesn’t feel like it’s even happened. Honestly, I’d like to live there. Rent is probably as much as the Grand National.      Let’s not pretend we could afford it—personally I’m just grateful I don’t own a car. No breakdowns, no insurance, no fancy trips to the local MOT centre risking getting run over by a penguin.      Speaking of vehicles, last night, my nephew was trying to tell me his new crush had a Volkswagen Golf and it was "so cool because American car measurements are massive." I looked at him like someone just told me Mars bars were now made from seaweed. He thought I was a relic— a relic at 46 . I want to send him a postcard from wherever people are taught how a litre about half a pint.      That’s just the tip of the iceberg though, isn’t it? I was trying to convince my eldest niece the other day that going abroad with her whole family every summer isn’t a given in most parts of the country. She looked at me like I told her the moon was made of cheese.      Honestly, the amount of stuff we take for granted. Websites like booking flights with lunches, hotels with “free parking,” and flights that don’t smell like someone’s packed a trapeze artist's dinner. Then go and pretend it’s life if you don’t get a refund for losing your dentures in transit.      Time to get philosophical, isn’t it? I was thinking the other night—do we ever live in the moment anymore, or just wait for holidays to feel alive?

Ugh, this weather’s doing my head in — it’s been nonstop rain for days. The first day of the kids' sports day and now they're stuck inside! Poor Mia was so excited about running that race.      Oh I know what you mean, love. I was in at eenie meenie’s last week and one of the mums said it rained all day on their sports day too. They just had to do it under a marquee, but it was alright. Still worth it to see the kids happy anyway.      Honestly, I thought it was going to hold off. I even baked mini scones for a picnic post-race, only to have to push them in the oven again today because they went rock solid left out in this damp! I’m not obsessed, I swear, but now I’m thinking of investing in one of them fancy dehumidifying ovens. Or maybe a drier!      Dehumidifying oven? That is a thing? They didn’t teach that in my college modules. Speaking of which, I was thinking, if I had one of those, would I actually be able to afford it? I live on a student budget!      You’d probably stretch your rhythm and then just have to borrow from mia – no chance of her saying no, least not if you mention her new potty-trained badge of honour.      Speaking of the potty! Liam’s still been having those little 'unannounced' episodes. Honestly, I think he just wants to test my patience. I buy all these cute ones — a dinosaur, a space rocket… Even a mini fridge — but he only ever fully enjoys the giraffe with the squeaky tail. I’m starting to think Build a Bear had it right — you can customise your teddy to be exactly the one your kid will fall for.      Oh I took Mia to Build a Bear last weekend actually. She picked out this unicorn named Sparklehoof and insisted it had to come to sports day. You know, just in case there was a rain cloud sprite to cheer her up.      That’s what I like to see — a child prepared for all eventualities. You know, I remember my sister giving me that really smelly foam rabbit that leaked blue ink once. Still, I slept with it for years. Sisterly relationships, I dunno, what can I say? We all have our weird legacies.      My sister and I never had that, but we still had our moments.

So do you think we could actually make this work?      Work what?      Living in Australia temporarily while I run the new business from here.      Well… I mean, I’ve always wanted to live in Melbourne. But it’s also not just about the holidays, is it? It’s about   us  .      I know. I’ve been thinking about this so much. I’m not interested in rushing into a new country just to do a business trip and leave. But this could be a stepping stone. The startup isn’t huge, but it’s stable enough to allow us to plan, and the idea of not being stuck in the same routine…      The same routine’s not been so bad, to be honest. I’ve settled in and I love the job I’ve got at the school. But I suppose if we’re talking long term, I do want more than a commute in traffic and dinner on tray tables.      Exactly. And I want to include you properly in this journey—career-wise, yes, but also in life. I don’t want to be one of those people who only calls on weekends.      I know. And I’d like to support you. But – what about my teaching contract? I still have two years left on it. And my mother’s health…      I know. And we don’t have to do it all in one go. We could rent a place for a year, a trial period. I can do the business remotely for the first few months, and you can still teach part-time if need be.      I like that. A trial. No pressure to leave the UK entirely. It gives us a chance to see if this is what we   both   want. And if we do, we can figure out the rest from there.      And if we don’t, we go back home and assume the commute was worth talking about.      As if that’s ever going to happen. No, this would be amazing. I’ve told my students I’m thinking about a sabbatical, something around teaching travel or environmental education—this could go hand in hand with it if you’re open to it.      I’m open to it. That might be something I can help with. The business could have a subsidiary or special projects—maybe something in education.      It’s a lot to talk about, but I’m into the idea.

Right, I just texted Rhian to see when she’s coming back from her smoke break. Honestly, I got to my half a cigarette before she dragged us all outside!      You’re doing it again with the cigarettes. Look, I’ve told you—my heart rate was in the 130s last week because of you and your Fitbit! My anxiety levels peaked when it sounded like that car alarm by Slade's side!      Yeah, yeah, easy for you to say, Sam. You don’t have a job where your Fitbit judges you every time you tense up. My Fitbit just tracked how much I paced around the kitchen after work thinking about whether I made that My Pokémon Scarlet save before I lost power!      I didn’t know Pokémon saved on Fitbits now!      It doesn’t, idiot. He just likes when you all listen to him monologue about Pokémon after I accidentally throw another After Eight at him!      Honestly, the only After-Eight I throw is at Mum when she asks if I’ve cleaned my room—again. I swear, even Dusty the cat knows when to ignore her!      Okay, circle back. What was the best way to camp at the Serv estate last weekend? I almost had to take off my boots because of the puddles. It was so much like when we stayed at that field near the Aura campsite—do you remember? They had that chicken curry for ten quid.      I remember. That was hotter than the fire at my Nan’s stew and it poured rain at like midnight! We all looked like drowned rats in about five minutes.      And the worst part is, I didn’t even take my Sat nav because I thought “I’ve driven it ten times before.” Wrong! I ended up in Burgess and had to get out my phone to ask for directions. Classic me.      At least you didn’t meet a family from South Korea there. We did last year and had that lovely exchange of sentences in broken English with lunches of kimchi and English digestive biscuits.      Okay, serious now—who wants to go the Costa by the go-kart track? My treat. I’m buying so I can ask Mark about how he got that gap year job in Brighton last summer. I’ve had enough of you two arguing about whether fluency in creoles counts as a degree!

Rather skip the new series of Doctor Who.      You’d think it'd be like... got to see it when it’s on because it’s been so long, but I think we’ve lost it this time.      Honestly, I wouldn’t miss it for the world if I didn't  have  to. Not like it used to be.      I’ve only watched a couple episodes this season. I got pulled into this documentary series on the Channel 4 about football and how it was run before the Premier League. Apparently, the owners used to rent out players like hotels.      Is that right?      Yeah! And that one chap, he was living in his car for a week because of a dispute with the manager. D’you know, I think he turned out alright—went on to win the league the next season.      Well, football stories always are like that. Full of drama and poor choices, really.      Good thing we’ve moved past that, right? Though I hear Championship clubs are still up to all sorts with land deals and planning applications. I tell you, it’s like they’re running a municipal company, not a football club.      Mate, I wouldn’t let football clubs anywhere near town halls if I were the PM. Now don’t get me started on their use of the internet and email. I saw the Prime Minister reply to a someone on Twitter last week—properly cheeky man.      Oh, you mean the one about her cat and the National Trust tea towel?      That’s the one. Lady who ran off with the goldfish from the Palace of Westminster this time. And I suppose you’re not surprised it wasn’t the actual cat?      I do miss proper leafy print Gazette. Smells like dust and tragedy, but at least it told you the football results on time.      Ah, but when I started doing this childminding, I could hardly afford to buy a paper. And frankly, I think it was better when I took the kettle off the boil and opened the paper with a bit of ceremony. No more goings-on on your own about something or other.      I was just telling Dad about this event we might host at the lecture hall. It’s themed around sustainability and local food. You know, sourcing everything from within a 50-mile radius.      Oh, very posh. We used to call that growing a vegetable in the allotment to make a tomato sausage.

So do you really think about dropping out?      I just can’t do it. I got to go home one weekend after the last assessment and I just fell apart.      What were you crying about exactly? Your results?      No, it’s not the results, I mean I got an E grade on that history module, but… it’s like I’ve been working so hard and I feel like I’m not getting anywhere. I watched my nan’s funeral two weeks ago and I was like, what’s the point of all of this?      That sounds really heavy. I can see why you’re struggling. Did you talk to anyone about it? My lectures are fine, but I still get left behind a lot.      I talked to the student support person, but I just don’t feel like they’ve got any better ideas than me. I’m thinking about just… returning home for a while and taking a year out.      I mean, maybe that’s actually the right thing to do? I tell you what, I’d rather be up here in this flat with your muddy boots and your grief than be back in Liverpool trying to pretend I’m okay while I work at a coffee shop.      Oh come on, I wouldn’t say it like that! But I get what you mean.      You know what I never understood? You’ve been called “Bluey” all your life and your name is Alice. Why’d your family call you that?      Haha, fair question. It comes from my mum – she had a horse when she was a kid, called Bluebell. Everyone just started calling me Bluey as a joke. I didn’t like it at first, but I got used to it. Why do you think I got to be “Ruby” for like four years?      Well that’s obvious, isn’t it? I was bloody red at birth, I looked like I’d been smothered in beetroot juice. My nan came in and said, “She’ll be Ruby Jane Granger from now on.”      Okay, that’s not bad. I wish my name was gothic or something. Alice Liverpool sounds like a cat walking over a keyboard.      Well you were born in Liverpool, so what can we do? So are you planning to seriously drop out and just take a break?      It’s not like I made peace with it over the weekend.

Victoria! Oh my god, it’s so good to see you. I was starting to think you’d forgotten I existed after all these months.      I know, I know! It’s a mad schedule at Pearson with all the marketing campaigns and the rebranding project. But honestly, we seriously needed this. How’s the project coordination life treating you?      It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I love the variety and the challenge, but sometimes I swear I have meetings every five minutes! It’s not like the peace and quiet of when we were uni students working part-time and barely surviving on beans.      That’s the truth. Still, you’ve always managed to juggle things like a pro. I still remember you pulling all-nighters in the library while I was out on the town. I think I turned into a wine-induced philosopher for about a year.      And then I’d see you with a massive hangover at the next seminar and just stare at you, thinking, “Is this the same human who lectured me about the meaning of life the night before?”      I know, I know. But seriously, I’ve started going to the gym a bit more—it’s the circle of life. Be healthy, get a job, start caring about yourself, right? Though I still live off chocolate and coffee. You?      Same, same. I’ve been trying to eat more greens, though, which is a joke because I still crave my mum’s lasagna like it’s the last one on Earth. Speaking of, did I tell you my sisters and I are being their unofficial matchmakers?      No, about time! Someone finally pulled the plug on the broken single life of Jane and Sam. I remember them both crying at Sarah’s wedding like they were the ones getting divorced.      Exactly! And guess what? My sister Jane actually passed on your friend Aiden’s number to Sam. She told him he was “hot, relatable, and not waiting for a phone call from 2004.” That’s a real compliment by the way.      Okay, if Aiden’s into it, maybe something will come of it! I owe you one. But really, Victoria, if you ever need a real friend who doesn’t just reply with “Text me harder,” I’m here.      Don’t worry, I’ve made it clear that this catch-up is now every three weeks, not every three years.

Right Aaron, I've just done my weekly sorting of post. There's a couple of parcels came in—seems like another one of them went missing on its way. Not sure what happens to them, but they’re always late when they do arrive.      Which one gone missing?      The  Legend of Zelda  one you ordered off eBay. I had a feeling they were a bit ambitious with the delivery estimates. Got one from Amazon, though. Oh, and your mum sent a reasonable little card and some chocolates. I hope you like the Lindt, or was it Cadbury?      Still mostly Lindt, I reckon. What's the鄣 deadline now for it to arrive? My mates are all waiting for it. I got it primed and ready, the case all cleaned, even made a place for it on the shelf.      Yeah? Well better late than never, eh? I just happened to read a bit in the paper the other day about eBay and Amazon, you know, those customer service complaints. One bloke said he waited nearly four weeks just for a book, and it was the wrong edition! Fancied himself to be buying grief when he opened it, he did. Still—it shows how popular these places are, from what I can see.      I reckon, but sometimes it just feels like buying something online and hoping it gets there somehow. I did that for a load of stuff for Science Fair. Ordered a screwdriver from this someone in Plymouth and never saw it. That made me a bit late for the display. Didn’t help my grade at all.      Sounds like a bit of a panic then, doesn’t it? I mean, I know I use it quite a lot for my lotions and things. I’ve got this dermatologist推荐 that I like and they only handle it through Amazon. Gets to me within a couple of days, usually. Doesn’t happen much here in Malton, but with deliveries like it, you get a nice surprise.      Yeah, I sort of stick to Amazon for stuff like that. They’ve never shorted me with what I need. eBay feels more like gambling, really. Like, you set a price, someone bits it and the next thing you go to collect it, it’s like antiques or something. But I guess you can get some really good deals.      Aye, if you know what you're doing.

Rather annoying isn't it, this weather.      It's like it's pretending to be spring and then it just dumps it all at once. I can't get my coat off, then it suddenly pours. Not to mention my commute is a nightmare at the moment.      That's the way of it. It was like that when I was still about as well. Though I used to take the tube. Not that that was much better, mind you. The old Northern Line was like a journey in itself.      Oh I can imagine. Still, at least you didn’t have to be anywhere  specific  when you retired. No real pressure to be anywhere on time unless you fancy a walk. I’ve still got to be at the office most mornings, unless I’m lucky enough for a home day.      It must be tiring working all day and coming home to Cambridge then. I mean, with all the tourists around at this time of the year. You never get to move for people in costume taking photos.      It can be a bit much, yes. Sometimes I wish I lived somewhere a bit more... normal. But Cambridge is Cambridge, you know? It’s got its own charm. Even when it’s raining. Though I do find it funny how people still dress like it's the 1990s and forget about the umbrella.      Bless ‘em. Still, you’d better look after this body of yours. I remember when I had my heart scare a few years back, I thought I was chucking it in early. Now I can’t walk up more than a flight of stairs without wheezing like I just ran a marathon.      Oh don’t say that. I’ve seen your legs—you are built for running! I mean it. You could run rings around most of us.      You're kind to say that. I used to be a footballer for a while, back in my younger days. Not for the pros, mind you. Saturday morning side in Morden.      Oh right? I didn’t know that. What position did you play?      A defender, mostly. Knew every inch of that pitch if I say so myself. Not much else I could do after work, really. Going out with blokes on a Saturday morning to shout at the lousy referee.      That does sound like fun, though. You should write a memoir. "From Retired Man to Defender of Morden: A Lengthy and Slightly Breathless Journey."

So do you lot reckon we're going to be flying on Christmas Day or are we gonna be stuck in a car park again trying to get home after the party at Claire's?      I told you, we’re not flying this year, not when Simon says the motorway gets backed up for three hours beginning at 12pm. It was ridiculous   last year  —we had to sleep on a layby with a fox watching us from the undergrowth. Pretty weird, but honestly,   the fox was probably more offended than we were.        Honestly, the fox has won too many times. I had one come into my café   last week  , and I swear it stood up on its hind legs at the front doorstep, probably judging my scones. I gave it a napkin for safety, in case it was sad or something.      That’s brilliant. I better start breakfast with a scone and a jam sandwich for the local wildlife if they start coming for the crumbs again.      Yeah, I mean, I would too, if I saw a fox wearing a Christmas sweater in November. My Nan put one on the one that walks by the garden. Hilarious. The fox looked like it had been dressed by someone who’d just got off the night shift at a bakery.   Speaker_4 :   Oh, I totally respect that. It’s not like we don’t have our own bush wildlife back home—we’ve got kangaroos in the car park near my bar. But they don’t wear jumpers, unless it’s a Halloween shirt hotter than the outback. So, real talk here—Christmas food: where are we heading? Prime rib? Apple and blackberry pie? Or does   someone   want the Mexican fusion this year?      No chance of that again. Last year I tried   tamales in a secret family recipe fusion thing  , and it ended up being something passed off to the ducks. They loved it. I did not. I think I had to relapse into spaghetti Bolognese just to get my tastebuds back on track.      Please, keep the spaghetti out of the Bolognese. We lost a relative after a Christmas tureen of the 'incorrect' gochujang Bolognese.      Speaking of relatives, are we still doing Aunt Sue’s themed Christmas Eve dinner? I can’t remember if it was “1980s” or “jungle buffet” last year?      It was definitely jungle, and there was a person dressed as a tree.

Right, so we've got about 40 minutes before we have to meet her in Chester. You sorted with the WhatsApp group, or shall I message her again?      I think we’re fine, don’t worry. I’ve seen the message—she says she'll meet us halfway. She’s probably already there, honestly. You both driving forwards at the same speed?      I said I'd swap off halfway. Got side effects from the motion-sickness pills, so I’ll drive back. You can drive in the middle. Is that cool?      Sounds good to me. I’ve been noticing how people do that voice thing, you know, when they try to sound posh? My uncle from Essex does it all the time. I find it ridiculous.      Oliver, you know how I feel about accents? I spend most of my editing job rewriting people who think they need to sound more 'polished'. Honestly, I’d rather hear a strong, clear accent than that mangled version of Received Pronunciation people try to pull off.      Yeah, I know what you mean. My Nan in Birmingham puts on a different accent when she’s talking on the phone. Pretends she’s from somewhere fancier. I always laugh. She says it's for the Baptists: “charity begins at Chapel”.      Haha, classic. But to be fair, I use different voices all the time when I’m designing character dialogue for games. Some people have no idea how accents can define a character. It just sells the world. You ever play something with no accent at all?      Ugh,  yes . There’s that one game about cosmic werewolves where everyone sounds like the Queen of England had a lisp. It made the whole thing feel like it was set in a drawing room, not space!      Should we put the heating up? It’s quite nippy in here. I can’t believe it’s April and we’re still wearing jackets.      I brought a thermos of tea as well. You want some, Jake? It’s proper builder’s brew but better than the instant stuff the cafe in Ruislip sells.      I owe you one. Thanks. You know, if you ever need someone to give your characters a line in Birmingham lingo, I could totally do that.      Mike, you could have been in the 11+ and we’d still be wondering what happened with your brain. But I’ll take you up on that—might give our villain a touch of Brummie menace.

So did you watch The Batman last night?      Yeah, it was mad awesome. Robbie got the role of Riddler now, so it's all murder scenes with those creepy puzzles.      Robbie? That's like, Edward Scissorhands gone mad, innit?      Yeah, you get that vibe he’s basically not all there. But I reckon that works for the Riddler.      I didn’t get to watch it yet. We had to revise for the physics mock instead. Apparently, the test's gonna have questions on waves and radioactivity.      Ugh, radioactivity? That’s the boring bit. My uncle still talks about that meltdowns like it’s the most dramatic thing ever.      Easier than A-level physics. I did Edexcel last year and they threw in quantum physics—like, what even  is  a wave-particle duality, you know?      Honestly, the only thing I remember is Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle, and that’s just because of the TV show.      Oh yeah, Breaking Bad. Have either of you heard the soundtrack? That music is lit, like, way better than most movie soundtracks.      Nah, I prefer something more instrumental. Like the Interstellar theme—man, that’s space-y.      Yeah, I love ambient music. Spent my weekend listening to Boards of Canada. It just gives that chill vibe.      You into electronic music then?      Most of it, yeah. I did remix a bit of a song for our school radio last term. You can hear it if you tune into 106.1 FM.      You’re doing your own radio show?! That’s proper cool.      Nah, just a snippet. It was something I did during the lockdown, tried using Logic Pro. Took me weeks to get it right.      That’s probably better than what I did during lockdown—YouTube tutorials on guitar. My fingers still remember those calluses.      You go, man. I tried to learn piano once, but my brother made fun of my fake Chopsticks. Never again.      Guitar’s a good start. If you get seriously into it, you could do AS Music next year, right?      I was thinking about it, but the exams are tighter than you’d expect. I’d have to compose something and get assessed.      And you have to do a concert too, innit? Imagine the nerves.      Yeah, but if you pick the right piece, it’s doable. The people who did ‘Mozart on the Moon’ got a gold.      Well, I’ll think about it. As long as it doesn’t clash with physics and English lit.

Right, so today was Balanceability day at school, and they had the whole gym full of colour zones—blue, green, yellow, red. I’m so proud I helped set it up after school last week. The kids were jumping all over those balance beams like trampolines.      Mummy, I did the green one and didn’t fall off! My friend Sophie fell over on a log. A big log. Not funny!      She screamed. It wobbled like it was a jelly.      Oh no, poor Sophie. But you did brilliantly, Lily. Did you make it to the end without using your hands?      Mm-hmm! I did! I made it to the bit where there were pretend rocks and I had to jump on them and I did!      I fell off and went into the cushion, and then Winnie said I was like a crash-test dummy.      That’s what teachers do when they fall? Are they crash-test dummies too?      Well, not exactly… I mean, we land a lot in PE, but only for dramatic effect.      Mummy, Mr West was doing Balanceability too. He pretends he’s got a wobbly leg because he’s trying to be funny. But Miss Patel said to him, “Don’t fall over or Lily will hit you with the beanbag.”      That’s what I would do!      I think he made it all the way across without falling. Maybe being older helps with balance? Maybe he’s a Balanceability expert.      Mummy, the red zone is only for Year 6s. It was like a wall that wobbles up and down.      My sister Amy said she’s going to do her own Balanceability club at home. She told me she’s going to use the wooden spoons and the trampoline.      Oh really? So she’ll be the next Balanceability grandmaster with wooden spoons and foam? Well, if she needs a partner, you can help her run it, Lily. Maybe you can even go in uniforms.      With beanbags and everything!      Mummy, today in Time to Talk, your friend Mrs Shaw said her house is being completely renovated. She’s moving into a new room with a swimming pool and a manmade waterfall? For real?      Mummy! A waterfall? Like, so there’s water going over rocks and into a pool and you can jump in?      Well, more of a fancy garden feature, probably. Not like a full waterfall, but maybe small. And she does have a pool now, yes.

So did you go for your run this weekend then?      Yeah, I did—finally got the motivation. I mean, I’m more of a “stroll in the park with a coffee” person, but the gym was feeling like a 🔥 prison this week.      Haha, yeah, I totally get that. I tried doing yoga instead—rolling around on a mat pretending I’m flexible. Not the best look, but it gave me a few Instagram stories.      Oh, I follow you! Didn’t even know that was you. You doing hot yoga or is it just you pretending to dead cat with a slight breeze?      Dead cat is a real pose, I’m telling you. I’m not pretending! I’m working on emotional detachment. But anyway, I think I turned my ankle—my left one’s a bit sore.      Oi! Be careful or I’m replying to your post with, “Your ankle says hi.”      That would be cruel—viral or not, I’d never recover.      Right, as for me, I ran around Regent’s Park—absolute pain—it was 14 degrees and then it started drizzling. I looked like a soggy biscuit, and I barely lasted 30 minutes.      Ugh, that’s rough. I blame the London weather—it always wants to put people out.      Tell me about it. It just wants to remind me that I’m still from Lewisham, and I don’t belong in premium outdoor gear.      I about blocked the sun last summer trying to look the part. Actually, I had to stop a kid handing me a cap because I was grimacing in the reflection.      Honestly, I’m trying to get into it for my dating life. You know, I told a guy I was into running and he said he used to meet his ex on the London Marathon course.      Oh no. And what did you do?      I asked if the ex was into bagels and he looked at me like I told him the sky was green. I think he stopped talking after that.      I tripped that boy harder with my boxset binging story. I told him I could sum up my relationships in 30-minute episodes. He asked what genre, I said “Dramedy with a side of regret.” He never asked why I was single again.      I think we’re both just doomed in the romance department. Maybe it’s time we did group dates—try a hen night and then tell everyone it was just a gathering before midnight.

Right then, John, take a seat lad. That pizza’s still steaming. You look like you could do with a bite after one of those Domino Drives. I can’t imagine how much time you spend buckled in that seat all week.      Cheers, Mrs. Steele. Got eeny weeny bit of a runner’s sore back from sitting all day. Almost as bad as after a log day at granddad’s.      BURNED. It was a dump of a journey wasn’t it, lad? Slingin’ pots about the countryside with a cow on my back, I’ve had worse. Though I don’t suppose you’ve driven a lorry before?      Nope, but I watched it last week on one of them documentaries on the telly, with the steer and the trailer lights and all. It looked mental, but kinda cool at the same time, Granddad.      Well, he’s not wrong. Your grandad hides it, but he’s a bit of a showoff, John. Showed me the time he nicked a cow out of the side of the trailer in a storm to save it from rain. Bit like a war story in farming country.      Aye, it was a red heifer with a fairly large case of diarrhoea, if you wanna get technical. Still don’t know how I did it with one hand on the wheel and the other trying to keep the beast out of the rain. But I did. That’s just a man and his log.      Fair play. So, what’s with the Domino Drives? I heard people talking about it at school about how you save up points for gold buggers or something.      It’s not   just   gold buggers, it’s a loyalty card system to collect points, like for every £1 you spend. Saves you money in the long run if you’re a frequent eater of takeaway pizza, which he very much is.      We had to do a project at school on how Websites and apps track your lunches to keep you coming back. They call it ‘customer retention’.      Pfft! Sounds fancy, but go on then, Mr. Tech Genius. If it wasn’t for Domino, you’d be out here without a slice of boxy pizza on a rainy Thursday night. Now tuck in before I save it all and eat it after I go to bed, like last week.      Know where you’re at, Mags.

Rather skip the pub tonight, eh? You know what a nightmare it gets on a Saturday with the uni students...      Oh, I wasn’t looking forward to it anyway. A bit much for me after a long week of lab work and meetings.      Honestly, it’s beginning to get a bit much. I mean, I enjoy the odd pint, but sometimes I just miss a quiet night in with decent music and no stubby lads shouting about quid pro quo.      Tell me about it. I swear half the people in the place think they’re in a three-star restaurant if they order a "gigantic cheese and onion soufflé".      Oh, bless them! I suppose they’re trying to be posh. I mean, what even is a "gigantic cheese and onion soufflé"? Just a dodgy quiche breakfast, really.      Haha, yeah. And I’m not getting into that fiasco ordering veggies either. One time I asked for "a side of steamed greens," and the lad behind the bar raised an eyebrow like I was speaking a different language.      Tell me about it! You’d think it'd be a little simpler by now. I mean – rocket, spinach, kale, mixed leaves, it's not like we're asking for somethin' that grows on the moon.      Still, the pubs around here in Cambridge do at least try to keep up with the times. I had a decent salad sourdough with my pint the other night.      Oh right – I heard about that place! The one with the open kitchen and the barista who takes the mickey out of your order. "Would you like your latte with that pint then?"      That's the one. But personally, I just like the ones with the big sofa, a decent menu, and a bit of character – something removed from all the student rowdiness.      Yeah, good pubs are hard to come by these days. More often than not, the only one left with character is the one run by an ex-firefighter who’s seen every celebrity you’ve ever heard go in and out with their partner-of-the-month.      Oh, I remember hearing about this place further out by the A11. The bar owner swore he’d made a special conservation sandwich for someone after spotting them on one of those celebrity chef shows. Or maybe it was just a dodgy meatloaf nobody wanted to touch.      I'm not going to lie, I kind of like the idea of that, though.

Right, so the next one is on the red cards, and we need one of us to shout it out... but don’t use any vowel sounds or rhyming words! Easier said than done, right?      No, and don’t forget — you can’t use any words that are in the category  at all . It’s like   Articulate   on acid.      Yeah, I got stuck on  wedding  last time and someone said  solemn  and I nearly had a heart attack. It’s like a minesweeper of language.      Aye, it’s the same as when I was trying to get my kids to guess  honeycomb  and they were like, “Is it to do with bees?” I couldn’t say a single word for ten minutes!      Oh, I remember that one! You just said  bzzzz  in your head the whole time and looked like you were daydreaming.      So what’s the word? Can we see it?      No! You have to wait for the clue-giver to start. Speaker_1, you’re up first. What’s the first clue?      Okay... um... let me read the card...  hmm ...  theft . All right, what can I use? Let me think...      Quick, just someone say  pocket !      No, hang on.  Theft —it’s a type of crime. Any word that means taking something  without permission .      Legally?      No!      Stealing then!      No, that’s the actual  word  itself.      This is the worst round ever. What about  hot ? Theft is  hot ?      Like  hot property ? No... wait,  hot steal ?      No, no, you’re going the wrong way. Try thinking of a synonym.      Oh! How about  mugging ?      No. It’s more general.      Shawty?      Oh my God, I am  not  helping with that!      Look, can I try one?      You can go if I say so.      Right, clue one:  Theft . Clue two:  Snatched, pilfered, lifted, swiped . Clue three:  Underhand.       Ohhh, I get it!      What?      It’s  skimming !      No, wait... not skimming! That’s like reading or money...      Women?      How did you even get that far?   Speaker_2  :  We do wordplay all the time at school with the kids — it’s part of our curriculum. Theft. Woman. The thief is... the woman?       That’s the weirdest logic I’ve ever heard.      That’s Welsh logic. Gill achieved through music.      Aww, aye. That’ll be your bingo round.      Alright, let’s try the next word. I need someone to guess this one. Speaker_4’s turn. Good luck.      Erm... what’s the word?

Right, I’m just saying, I do not understand how you manage to lose in this game  every. Single. Time.  Someone teach me their secrets because clearly this is a murder cover-up.      Div, honestly, you sound like a maths teacher —  Pause.  Div was my old eeny weeny  welsh teacher  when I was little. Everyone thought I was going blind because I kept asking, “Miss, what's that number again?”           Please! You were the one who once called the Queen of Hearts “Her Majesty the Blob” because the head looked like baked custard. Still works, TBH.      Okay, well Myron, if I’m being accused of not having a poker face, I’m calling the police, and they’d better be in fake tails and playing cards with them too — or I’m not talking.      Well, no matter — in my day, we didn’t need fancy hides or blabs, we had the Real Thing. That card game was like Watergate with jokers and betting cups of tea.      What did you play back in the day, Nann? Snap on a bus or what?      You sarcastic young man — it was Royal Whist, and I had cards  polished  like a new pin. All that hand rubbing and card wiping was for the best!      Honestly, this is the best afternoon of my life. All my uncles and half my cousins are at the pub, and here I am with a tea-soaked grandma, an immigrant teacher,  and  a Welsh card expert who flinches at every “J” card.      I'm a  British citizen , thank you very much. I left South Africa when I was 18. My accent is for show and treacle scones.      Oh,  yer  a South African, oh bless. I could stick a sprig of heather on yer head and call yer a Londoner and a half.      Okay, well you  are  a man who once referred to his entire family gothic room as “Dumbledawk’s Den of Dodgy Goo.” You sure you’re from  anywhere  with standards?      Now listen all — enough chatting! If we carry on like this, we’ll never finish this round, and I promised myself a brand new zero-deck hand shuffle when we moved on to the next game. I’ve been practicing like a proper Welsh national.      Right, right — Nann, when you say “zero-deck hand shuffle,” are we expecting a conjuring act or just a bit of magic smoke and jokers?

Okay, so I've just watched this whole series of "Bridgerton" and it's so good... but honestly, half of me is like, "This would never happen in real life," and the other half is just like, "More corsets, more drama!"      Yeah, I saw the first two seasons and then got bored with it. I mean, I get it—it's a bit of a guilty pleasure. But I’d rather just binge something like _The Queen’s Gambit_ or something. You know, something with a bit more depth?      Honestly, I can’t even watch it without pausing because I keep thinking, “What’s that drink called again? Is that tea? Is it coffee? Is it some weird rich person wine?” I’m so out of my depth in these shows.      You’re all thinking too much about the fantasy part. Why do you think it’s working so well? Because people want to escape. People want to dream. Me, I’m ordering myself pizza and watching it. Good for the soul, I think.      Well, speaking of escaping, I’m seriously nervous about starting my traineeship next week. Honestly, I’ve never even touched an accounts system. I’m sure I’ll get it, but – yikes.      My sister just started her first year at uni and she’s already moving out next year. Honestly, I can’t imagine doing that. What if she hates it? Who am I gonna complain about the boring lectures to?      I mean, what if she’d rather have a nightmare roommate than you being her emotional support at university?      Don’t be mean! She’s not the verbal kind anyway. She’s like “quiet vibes only.” But you know what? I envy her. I’m stuck delivering Christmas cards up and down to the shops, like for the next month. It’s so much better than working on the tills again. I’d rather have frostbite than deal with disappointed customers at this time of year.      At least you’ll have warm clothes. I’m going out to a base in Portsmouth next week for some training simulation work. Sub-zero, no idea what it’s like, but I can go onboard a ship pretending it’s a spaceship or whatever.      Wait, you design spaceship systems?      No, no, no. Combat systems. Tanks, ships, submarines—basically everything that goes boom with a budget and a name like Project Thunderclap or something.

Rather annoying isn't it, eh? You can’t even get anywhere without people cycling down the dual carriageway and not blinking when they're doing it. Blows their horn, like we’re not there.      No, I mean—some people  do  use the proper cycle routes, but there  are  a lot who take   shortcuts  , basically. It’s not just a Cambridge thing, though. I see the same in Brighton, where I used to work.      Well, nothing was like this when  I  was walking or cycling as a kid. You just went down the High Street, made sure no one was coming and just crossed. Didn’t have lights or anything.      Oh, left-right-left—what do I need lights for? Drove without them for thirty years. Never had a problem.      Yeah, I see people old and young just cycling into junctions without looking. It’s not even the cyclists—it’s the drivers who flash them and get shouty. I had one bloke nearly give me a heart attack the other day.      Aye, people don’t like being passed, especially if someone’s on a bike. I saw a guy in a Range Rover nearly run someone off the road the other week because they didn’t stop at the junction long enough.      You know what gets me? If I’m already waiting at the zebra, and some twerp on a Lime bike zips across while I’m halfway across. Rude.      Also, some of the cycle paths in central Cambridge split off and twist back on themselves, so you can get about five people pedalling in the same direction the wrong way. It’s mind-bending if you don’t grow up with that sort of thing.      You’re not wrong, love. When I first moved here, I passed a lorry that just turned into a cycle lane without a thought. Nearly took the girl’s leg off.      This is why I prefer driving. At least you know where you are.      That’s if the drivers aren’t distracted trying to park around here. Sometimes I think the only thing goin’ on in Cambridge is people trying not to hit one another.      You know what the worst thing is though? Lift your legs when you cross at the lights. I’ve seen people with one bike wheel on the zebra and the other in the path of a bus.      Which reminds me—I went to walk the dog this morning near Grantchester and got stuck behind an old man in loafers trying to cycle on a Segway.

Rather skip the queue and just go through the side doors, do you need a coffee or would you rather get straight in?      I’m more than happy to take a coffee break first, I was doing a full run of lectures this morning and I’ve barely picked up my phone.      I won't pretend I’m not sorely tempted to sit this alumni nonsense out. Far too many of these things in my day—too many too-nice biscuits and too little information.      Please! You lectured me on the history of medieval law, don't say you won’t appreciate the tour of the Law Faculty. Besides, I heard they’re displaying some of the first printed legal journals from the 1500s somewhere in the archives. It could be fun, right?      Fun and I haven’t spoken in decades. But if it’s a brisk tour with something worth talking about afterwards then I’m in. I suppose I could stand a cup of tea and a biscuit, though not the kind they hand out in these things.      Fair point, those biscuits usually come with a side of guilt if you’re not careful. So, I assume you two have still been in touch about the linguistics circle? I remember when we got that funding from the ESRC back in ’02, still think it was the best thing we ever pulled off.      Oh yeah, we're still in contact with the old gang, and the Basque group in Spain still emails me every now and then about a new dictionary project they’re on. Some of them are out near Donostia these days. Still surprising to see where research leads people, really.      I hear Basque is such a tough one to crack. It doesn’t fit comfortably into any other linguistic family. I know some people who have moved out there for years to study just a tiny bit of it. Envy their ability to learn it with that kind of dedication.      Oh, it is intense, but there’s something incredibly rewarding about speaking a language that’s as ancient as it is stubborn. I always tell the students, a little bit of Basque goes a long way—it's like trying to speak a stone wall.      I remember when I visited your research partners in Spain. You two were always slipping off in separate directions, between Spanish tapas, tapas, and whatnot.
